semantic_review: Word width uses storeFormat, so bool is all256 raw signed i8 patterns rather than BitVec1. Other canonical signed/unsigned widths are source widths.
decodeCell binds the whole tagged cell; InputWords excludes active wrong-tag/default-value behavior. Unsigned cells use nat and signed/bool cells use int.
loaded_decode proves the raw-word load relation; bool zero/nonzero covers the sign-bearing raw byte, including 0xff→true.

resultWord preserves promotion-width casts and modular addition from original IntegerSource.resultCell, then encodes original x storage width. No floating callback or memory/execution reference occurs in the result formula.
stored_decode and storage_roundtrip preserve complete output storage. Bool+integer can store raw3; bool+bool wraps at compute i1 before reencoding signed8.
wordSpec uses initial words with a full outside-output/N frame. Full ordered grid success comes from the already-proved source runGrid, not equality of failures.

Both complete InputWords premises are explicit. Equal logical x/y names are allowed only when decoded input cells agree; withInputs_y states exactly this necessary compatibility, rather than introducing a distinctness guard.
Output aliases of input regions retain prior disjoint-tile logical-grid argument. No shifted/mixed-width physical byte-alias or native concurrency claim follows.
The public contract refines the existing81 integer/bool profiles only; no dtype pair or whole-original-program acceptance increment is claimed.

limits_confirmed.gap: Native memory to finite word input relation
limits_confirmed.detail: BitVec source widths and complete logical input tags are formal. Actual byte assembly/endianness, native load validity and source dtype dispatch satisfying InputWords remain unproved.
Input compatibility handles identical logical names. Shifted/misaligned/mixed-width physical byte views, allocation bounds/layout/freshness and race behavior remain outside the logical-cell model.

limits_confirmed.gap: Finite addresses, native errors and scheduling
limits_confirmed.detail: Positive natural block and ascending grid do not prove native block domain, zero-grid behavior, signed offset/pointer overflow, sanitizer/compiler admission/errors or native interleavings.
This refines the same81 integer/bool profiles and adds no dtype pairs. All other dtype/error families, original host/harness/module behavior and their native correspondence remain required.
